leftEvidence.title: Adam’s generations end with his death

points.label: Descendants named
points.left: The genealogy recalls image, male and female, blessing, and the name Adam, then records Seth in Adam’s likeness, other children, nine hundred thirty years, and death.
points.right: A prayer recalls Adam’s rule over creation and names both Israel and other nations as coming from him before asking why other nations now rule.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Children, generations, and death · core · Genesis 5:1–5
points.right: Adam in 2 Esdras · later memory · 2 Esdras 6:53–59

payload.posture: Seth, other sons and daughters, years, and death belong to Adam’s genealogy is held beside Israel and the other nations are both said to come from Adam.

rightEvidence.title: Adam is remembered as ruler and ancestor

payload.tension: Genesis begins a family line, while 2 Esdras uses shared descent inside a question about nations and inheritance.
payload.title: Adam’s descendants in Genesis and 2 Esdras
